_note: Newspapers.com clippings found and clipped by Michiko Quinones (1838 Black Metropolis), Nov. 2, 2026: United States Gazette and Philadelphia Inquirer items on Bethel Church, 1817-1827. Transcribed from the clipping images (clippings/); fixed person ids for the 1817 committee where Winch has the man (Francis Perkins: Winch notes his 'Committee of Eleven'). Robert Gordon and James Johnson left in the text only (several Winch men of each name). Newspapers.com image ids in each description.

events.name: Meeting of the people of colour at Bethel Church against colonization (January 1817)
events.description: "At a numerous meeting of the People of Colour convened at Bethel Church, to take into consideration the propriety of remonstrating against the contemplated measure, that is to exile us from the land of our nativity; JAMES FORTEN was called to the chair, and RUSSEL PARROTT secretary." Resolutions adopted with only one dissenting voice, rejecting colonization: 'we never will separate ourselves voluntarily from the slave population in this country; they are our brethren by the ties of consanguinity, of suffering, and of wrongs.' A committee of 11 was appointed to open a correspondence with the Hon. Joseph Hopkinson, member of Congress from this city, and to call a general meeting when needed: Rev. Absalom Jones, Rev. Richard Allen, James Forten, Robert Douglas, Francis Perkins, Rev. John Gloucester, Robert Gordon, James Johnson, Quamoney Clarkson, John Somerset, Randall Shepherd. Signed James Forten, Chairman; Russell Parrott, Secretary. Printed in the United States Gazette (Philadelphia), Aug. 13, 1817, p. 2. Courtesy Newspapers.com (clipped by 1838 Black Metropolis, Nov. 2, 2026). Clipping: clippings/USG_1817-08-13_p2_anti-colonization.jpg (Newspapers.com image 605091990).

events.name: Meeting of the free people of colour at the School house in Green's Court: Address against colonization (August 10, 1817)
events.location: School house in Green's Court, Philadelphia
events.description: "At a numerous meeting of the Free People of Colour of the city and county of Philadelphia, held, in pursuance of publick notice, at the School house in Greens Court, on the evening of August 10th, for the purpose of taking into consideration the plan of Colonizing the Free People of Colour of the United States on the coast of Africa: JAMES FORTEN was appointed Chairman, and RUSSEL PARROTT Secretary." The meeting adopted the Address 'To the Humane and Benevolent Inhabitants of the City and County of Philadelphia', disclaiming any wish to join 'the American society for colonizing the free people of colour of the United States' and warning that colonization would leave the enslaved 'more secure' in bondage. Signed James Forten, Chairman; Russell Parrott, Secretary. United States Gazette (Philadelphia), Aug. 13, 1817, p. 2. Courtesy Newspapers.com (clipped by 1838 Black Metropolis, Nov. 2, 2026). Clipping: clippings/USG_1817-08-13_p2_anti-colonization.jpg.

events.name: Committee of vigilance of thirty appointed at Bethel Church (1822)
events.description: "At a numerous meeting of the people of color convened at Bethel Church, a committee of vigilance, thirty in number, was appointed to co-operate with the Mayor and other officers of the police in any manner which they think will conduce to put an end to the depredations so frequently committed on the citizens. The meeting recommended to their brethren of color such demeanor as will secure the approbation of the public." Philadelphia Inquirer, Mar. 6, 1822, p. 2. (Poulson's American Daily Advertiser of Mar. 2, 1822 names Richard Allen chairman and Russell Parrott secretary.) Courtesy Newspapers.com (clipped by 1838 Black Metropolis, Nov. 2, 2026). Clipping: clippings/PI_1822-03-06_p2_committee-of-vigilance.jpg (Newspapers.com image 346667519).

events.name: Cayenne pepper outrage at Bethel Church; Catharine Williams killed (November 20, 1825)
events.description: "Disgraceful Outrage. On Sunday evening, some white young men entered the Bethel African Church, nearly at the close of the services, and deposited in the stove, a quantity of Cayenne pepper and salt, and retreated; the effect of this mixture when operated upon by the heat, was soon manifested by the coughing and sneezing of the audience, and the excessive difficulty of breathing. In the midst of this trouble the cry of fire was raised, and the whole congregation rushed towards the different doors; in the hurry to escape, all order of course was disregarded, and hundreds lay prostrate upon the floor, with other hundreds treading upon them. We hear that Catharine Williams died immediately after being removed from a heap of fallen bodies. Another died yesterday morning and many more are dangerously injured." United States Gazette (Philadelphia), Tuesday morning, Nov. 22, 1825, p. 2. Courtesy Newspapers.com (clipped by 1838 Black Metropolis, Nov. 2, 2026). Clipping: clippings/USG_1825-11-22_p2_bethel-pepper-outrage.jpg (Newspapers.com image 605129524).
attendees: killed in the crush (died after being removed from a heap of fallen bodies)

events.name: Public meeting of the people of colour at Bethel Church on the kidnappings (February 5, 1827)
events.description: "PUBLIC MEETING. A public meeting of the People of Colour, will be held at Bethel Church on Monday evening, at 7 o'clock, for the purpose of adopting such measures, as may be deemed necessary for the apprehension and conviction of the persons concerned in the abduction of several people of colour from this city." Philadelphia Inquirer, Sat. Feb. 3, 1827, p. 2, repeated Mon. Feb. 5, 1827, p. 3. Courtesy Newspapers.com (clipped by 1838 Black Metropolis, Nov. 2, 2026). Clippings: clippings/PI_1827-02-03_p2_kidnapping-meeting.jpg clippings/PI_1827-02-05_p3_kidnapping-meeting.jpg (Newspapers.com images 346705616, 346705664).

events.name: Bethel Church appoints a committee of vigilance of twenty against kidnapping (February 1827)
events.description: COMMUNICATION. "The congregation of the African Methodist Episcopal Bethel Church, were on last Sabbath day after divine service, informed by R. Allen, pastor of the said church, that he had received from his Hon. Joseph Watson, Mayor of this City, an advertisement concerning a number of coloured children that had been kidnapped from this city and county, and sold into slavery." The congregation was admonished to be aware how and to whom they bound their children. It thanked the Mayor, Select and Common Council, Messrs. Hamilton and Henderson of Rock Spring, Mississippi, and Messrs. Holmes, Davis and Walker of Natchez, for their efforts to return the children to their parents and bring the kidnappers to punishment. "A committee of vigilance consisting of twenty persons of colour have been appointed to aid in the detection of those offenders, and to give all and every necessary information to the civil authorities of this city." United States Gazette (Philadelphia), Feb. 23, 1827, p. 4. Courtesy Newspapers.com (clipped by 1838 Black Metropolis, Nov. 2, 2026). Clipping: clippings/USG_1827-02-23_p4_committee-of-vigilance.jpg (Newspapers.com image 605005093).
attendees: pastor of Bethel; read the Mayor's notice to the congregation (printed 'R. Allen')

events.name: Report of the Special Vigilance Committee: support for the Christiana prisoners (Frederick Douglass' Paper, March 4, 1852)
events.description: A report of Philadelphia's Special Vigilance Committee, printed in Frederick Douglass' Paper (Rochester, N.Y.), Thursday, March 4, 1852, page 1, column 3 ('Report'). It shows the committee providing support for the people held in jail while awaiting trial after the Christiana resistance of September 11, 1851 (identified by Michiko Quinones, Nov. 2, 2026). The committee's names and figures have not yet been transcribed here from a full-resolution copy. Source: Frederick Douglass' Paper, courtesy New York Heritage Digital Collections, St. John Fisher University (https://nyheritage.org/organizations/st-john-fisher-university); the item is also catalogued by House Divided, Dickinson College (https://hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu/node/21091).
